LPSTB and RES input buffers: left cell LPSTB, right cell RES; each a small inverter then a two-finger inverter, so the core sees the pin level
LPSTB and RES input protection: two mirrored comb cells; left serves LPSTB, right serves RES
input buffers: CLK and E: three-finger inverter then two-finger inverter. R/W, RS, CS: chain of four inverters each, both polarities available. One more inverter at the left end
input protection: five clamp cells in order CLK, R/W, E, RS, CS; each pad reaches its cell through a resistive strip
main clock buffer: CLK pin node drives a three-stage buffer (two big inverters, then a push-pull pair). Output is NOT CLK, the main internal clock
clock gate row: six inverters: two pairs delay each clock phase for the other half of the generator; one pair sits across the two phase lines
clock wiring: lines A, B, their re-buffered copies, buffered CLK and the CLK pin node on their way down; six small clamp devices to VCC
two-phase clock generator: two cross-coupled NOR drivers: ck_a (high only while CLK low) on the left, ck_b (high only while CLK high) on the right, with an inverter for NOT CLK in the middle
data bus interface: column of logic beside the D0-D7 pads
D0-D7 pad cells: eight identical cells, 1600-1735 px apart: tri-state driver with its pre-driver under the VCC band, input protection above. Located, not yet fully traced (AMB-003)

register decode: 7 6 4 0 2 1 10 5 3 8 9 11 13 12 14 15 17 16: NOR array, 5-bit address to 18 register selects. Columns left to right select R7 R6 R4 R0 R2 R1 R10 R5 R3 R8 R9 R11 R13 R12 R14 R15 R17 R16. Nothing decodes addresses 18-31
top-left logic: random logic
top-centre logic: random logic left of the central datapath
left-centre logic: random logic between the left array and the central datapath
top-right logic rows: two rows of gates under the test structures, near the RA/HSYNC/VSYNC pads
logic above mid-right array: small array, 4 or so columns
bottom-centre logic: random logic below the central datapath
bottom-left logic: random logic near DISPTMG/CUDISP pads
strobe channel: 18 vertical tracks: register strobes R0-R7 go north from here into the right datapath's left bundle
gate column left of the select gates: one column of gates; includes the driver of the signal that the clock block's lone inverter receives

svg.text: gate column left of the select gates ?

rect.title: logic right of the select gates: random logic; the write strobe arrives from here

svg.text: logic right of the select gates ?

rect.title: small cell by die marking: isolated cell left of the HD46505S text
bus field: dense horizontal wiring between the left array and the rest
top-right bus field: horizontal buses under the test structures
bottom bus field: wiring along the bottom of the core
process test structures: devices labelled E, A, S, D with probe pads
die marking: HD46505S and mask revision marks
Address row inverters (x5): make the complement row of each decode row pair from the true row; not a register
Address lines to the row inverters: four metal lines from the register cells above the decode array plus one poly line, as nested poly L shapes

svg.text: Address lines to the row inverters

rect.title: Address register bit (fifth of five): latch written from a data line through a pass transistor gated by the load strobe; drives decode row pair 4. Partly traced
Address feeds and load strobe bundle: ar1..ar4 feeds, the address register load strobe (metal x 16299, from below), two more lines to the right-hand column

svg.text: Address feeds and load strobe bundle

rect.title: Column of cells right of the bundle: four identical cells then larger ones; not traced

svg.text: Column of cells right of the bundle ?

rect.title: row D strobe drivers (bc1): two strong inverters with one input: one drives cdp4_ld6 (strobe of the 6-bit latch row D), the other a twin line going up at x 7448
strobe NAND (bc1): 2-input NAND of two channel lines; the strobe is their AND
2-bit decoder (bc1): two bus lines (y 14832, 14873) inverted and decoded by three NANDs into active-low lines for 00, 10 and 01
inverter, weak load (bc1): input from below the block, output to the gates under it
13-line bus: horizontal metal lines from the left field towards the right; the two lowest drop into the decoder
row D data lines: six poly lines carrying the data inputs of the 6-bit latch row D of the central datapath
write strobes turning north: sel_w6 w1 w2 w0 w4 arrive in poly and each ends on a contact under a track of the 18-line bundle (x 13088-13826) that carries it north
track channel: 18 vertical metal tracks with poly cross-unders; sel_w5 and sel_w7 climb it from the bottom and leave north on tracks k1, k2; other lines go into the mid-right array
two inverters on line X: both driven by X (the input of input-row gate 0); outputs NOT X leave north on track k6 and south on x 13716
inverter of bd1_a: bd1_an = NOT bd1_a; output goes south on a metal line (x 13783) to the latch's lower half
latch gated by NOT X, upper half: bd1_n1 = NOT(bd1_a.bd1_xn2 + bd1_q); output on a metal line x 13957

svg.text: latch gated by NOT X, upper half

rect.title: pull-down of bd1_k: gate bd1_g (the input of X's driver)
latch gated by NOT X, lower half: bd1_n2: pull-downs bd1_an.bd1_xn2 and bd1_n1 traced; its load (north-east, y 15640-15705) not traced

svg.text: latch gated by NOT X, lower half

rect.title: gate column, untraced part: gates under the ground rail x 13848; ck_out tap at y 15930
driver of line X: one inverter, X = NOT g; g arrives in poly along y 16231 from a line at x 13630
gate column, untraced part: gates; ck_out taps at y 16490, 16565, 16711
write strobes from below: sel_w7 w5 w3 w8 from bd3: w7 and w5 turn north into the channel, w3 goes north in poly, w8 west in poly along y 17125
Write strobe driver: inverter: sel_stb_r = NOT bd2_n1 (the strobe latch); output north and west to the register select gates
Address register load driver: inverter: areg_load = NOT bd2_al_n = bd2_x OR (E AND write to the address register); output up the bundle to the address register

Write strobe latch: D latch open while E is high: two cross-coupled AND-OR-invert gates plus the inverter of its data input; holds "write to a data register" through E low; its Q drives the write strobe driver
Strobe and E bundle: areg_load and sel_stb_r up, E (x 16169) from below, latch data input (x 16277) and its inverse (x 16104)
Address load gate: under a ground rail: bd2_al_n = NOT(bd2_x OR (E AND bd2_m210)) for the address register strobe, and bd2_nu = NOT(bd2_c AND E); loads and inputs from the east not traced
Data register write decode: 3-input NOR of R/W, NOT RS and CS: write AND chip selected AND RS high; data input of the write strobe latch
Address register write decode: 3-input NOR of R/W, RS and CS: write AND chip selected AND RS low; gates the address register strobe
RS inverter and R/W gate: top gate pulled low by RS (its output is the NOT RS of the data register decode); the gate below it takes R/W: not traced
R/W, RS, CS and E risers: E (x 16169), R/W (x 16298, ends y 16040), RS (x 16342, ends y 16603), CS (x 16385, ends y 16171), with the decode outputs between them

svg.text: R/W, RS, CS and E risers

rect.title: Bus control gate column, lower part: not traced

svg.text: Bus control gate column, lower part ?

rect.title: Right-hand column and routing: not looked at
R12 select buffer: two inverters: rsel12 buffered, leaves south in poly at x 14199 (?read enable of R12)
write strobes R12, R13: inverter + NOR with the strobe, as for R14/R15; outputs down the tracks at x 15214 and 15344
R13 select buffer: two inverters: rsel13 buffered, leaves south in poly at x 15512 (?read enable of R13)
middle bundle, lower part: T0 (strobe) ends; T1-T6 turn west; T7/T8 selects end at their gates; write strobes and buffered selects go on south
write strobes going west: sel_w5 w3 w8 w9 w11 w10 on metal at y 17041-17258, crossing the supply rail x 14609 in poly; the strobe's poly link to the left strobe line along y 16996
write-strobe driver: one big inverter: strobe = NOT E (e_b); feeds the 16 strobe gates, so each register's write strobe is (selected) AND E
strobe to the select gates: poly y 14825, metal y 14872, poly x 16259 from the driver's output
VSS feeds and band: three feeds from the VSS plane and the band joining the slice rails; row A's outputs leave upward here

R8 register (6 bit): six static register bits (write pass transistor, two inverters, grounded-gate feedback). Each output leaves upward on its own wire. Three bits share a bit line with the register below, three do not; R8 is believed from that and the width
compare bit 5 detour: two poly lines: the 5-bit register's fifth bit goes west to the island at x 7330-7900 and comes back, modified, to the comparator
5-bit equality NOR: one pull-down per slice on a diffusion line along the row, load in the left slice; output leaves west along y 4459. High when the register below equals the compare value
comparator XOR (5 bits): per bit NOR(A,B) and an AND-OR-invert: differs = A XOR B, A the register bit, B a line from the channel below
compare value (5 lines): five poly lines from the east, one per comparator bit; also the feed of one bit line of the 6-bit register from the west
5-bit register: five static register bits, same cell as the row above; outputs go up to the comparator. Which register is not known yet
data bus channel: fourteen poly lines; each bit line of the two registers meets one line that runs east (believed the data bus), seven lines pass through
rows D and E (5 cells): not traced

5-bit register latch row: five static latch bits (pass transistor from the per-slice data bus line, two inverters, weak hold device), loaded together by one strobe line. Outputs q go up to a comparator in the rows above. Which register: not yet established

comparator operand lines: five long poly lines carry a 5-bit value to the through tracks of the slices, which take it up to the rows above and down to the comparator below; the q tracks of the latch row cross them

7-bit register latch row: seven copies of the same static latch cell with their own strobe line. Five bits feed the comparator above, the two leftmost bits leave to the left. Which register: not yet established (the 5 + 2 split would fit R10)

5-bit comparator of the register below: per bit: XOR of the register bit with the bit on the slice's through track, a chain from left (most significant) to right, and a pull-down on a row-long line. Believed outputs: "equal" at the right end of the chain, "greater" on the line; one connection per bit not seen
channel 2: 13 horizontal poly lines under the per-slice metal lines and rails; the lowest carries the comparator's chain output
row of large cells below the 7-bit register: six slices, continues below y 8450 (cdp3's row A); fed by the data bus lines only from above. Not traced

svg.text: row of large cells below the 7-bit register ?

rect.title: channel 3: five horizontal poly lines across the array, no contact seen in the slices looked at
read gates onto bus N (rows E, F): two pass transistors per column: gate_e puts the six row C register bits (and 0 in the two left columns) on bus N, gate_f the eight row H values

svg.text: read gates onto bus N (rows E, F)

rect.title: row C register outputs going west: six poly lines, one from each row C cell (true data, buffered) to the west edge

svg.text: row C register outputs going west

rect.title: channel G tracks: per column: one poly line between the west edge and the row H cell, and the column's bus N line leaving east

6-bit read/write register (row C): static register cell per column c2..c7: written from the column bit line when the write line is high, held through a grounded-gate device; one buffered output west, one onto bus N. Believed R12 or R14 (high bits)

8-bit read/write register (row H): the row C register cell upside down in all eight columns, on the same bit lines, with its own write line; outputs west on the channel G tracks and onto bus N. Believed R13 or R15 (low byte)
row A cells (6 bit): large cell per column c2..c7, on the same bit lines as the two registers, with one line each from the west and one output (line f) going south; not traced

channel B tracks and links: six poly lines from the west, one into each row A cell; short poly links take a second line of each row A cell onto vertical line f, which runs down through row C to the rows below

NAND beside the row C register: two-input NAND (inputs: a poly line from the west edge at y 9450 and a metal line from above at x 8327); its output is on line e of column c1 and on a line going up at x 7880

svg.text: NAND beside the row C register

rect.title: 8-bit latch (selector source b): the register latch cell upside down: strobe line along its bottom edge, data tracks from the row above, buffered output down to the selector
channel 1: per-slice lines to the left: eight poly lines from the left edge, one per slice, each tapped by a vertical metal that goes up into the row above

svg.text: channel 1: per-slice lines to the left

rect.title: 4-way read selector (8 bit): four pass transistors per slice put one of four sources on the output node n: a and c are 6 bits wide (slices s2-s7, the two left slices strapped to VSS), b and d 8 bits; select lines sel1-sel4 come from the left
selector output pull-down: per slice a transistor from n to VSS gated by one line (rst) from the left

8-bit latch (selector source d): pass transistor loaded from the left by strobe ld, two inverters, and a buffer inverter that drives the selector; same cell family as the right datapath's register latch
channel 2: latch data in, selector out: per slice one poly line in two pieces: from the left edge to the latch input, and from the selector node n to the right edge (towards the data bus)

svg.text: channel 2: latch data in, selector out

rect.title: 6-bit latch (selector source c): six latch cells under slices s1-s6, strobe from a contact at the left end, data tracks leave the bottom of the array; each buffered output is linked in poly to the c track of the next slice to the right
D0 input buffer: four inverters in series from the D0 pad (d0_a..d0_d), like the R/W, RS, CS buffers; only d0_d, the delayed pad level, feeds logic
D1 input buffer: same cell; input traced from the D1 pad
D2 input buffer: same cell, assigned by position
D3 input buffer: same cell, assigned by position
D4 input buffer: same cell, assigned by position
D5 input buffer: same cell, assigned by position
D0 buffer capacitors: plain diffusion rectangles for d0_b (contact cut, not strapped) and d0_c
D0 bus gating and read driver: NAND and AND-OR-invert pull-downs seen under the ground rail; takes d0_d, drives the per-bit line to the D0 pad cell; not traced

svg.text: D0 bus gating and read driver ?

rect.title: D1 bus gating and read driver: looks like a copy of the D0 group; not traced

svg.text: D1 bus gating and read driver ?

rect.title: D2 bus gating and read driver: looks like a copy of the D0 group; not traced

svg.text: D2 bus gating and read driver ?

rect.title: D3 bus gating and read driver: looks like a copy of the D0 group; not traced

svg.text: D3 bus gating and read driver ?

rect.title: data bus control logic: single gates on a 152 px pitch, not surveyed
pad driver lines: P_x, one metal line common to all eight data pad cells (enable), and the per-bit lines and pad input lines beside it

14-bit counter: incrementer and stored bit (14 rows): per row: carry = carry-in AND Q, sum = carry-in XOR Q by pass gates, all-ones line per group; the bit is a static pair with a weak hold device. Believed the MA counter. Traced

svg.text: 14-bit counter: incrementer and stored bit (14 rows)

rect.title: counter latch stage (14 rows): dynamic node X1 takes the incremented value (strobe Vm2) or a value from the right (Vm3); inverter; pass gate to Y (Vm5); write gate of the stored bit (Vm6); clear (Vm1). Traced
counter rows, middle part (14 rows): Y ends on a gate here, Z (the value written back) and the load value come from here; a wide driver on rail F. Not traced
MA row cells, right column (14 rows): one cell per counter row; not looked at

svg.text: MA row cells, right column (14 rows) ?

rect.title: carry gap 1: carry out of bits 0-6 leaves here, carry into bit 7 arrives; horizontal poly bands
carry gap 2: carry out of bits 7-9; all-ones line of bits 7-9 becomes carry into bit 10

left column beside the arrays: cells on the row boundaries; the inputs of the MA8 and MA9 output drivers end in the cells at the s4/s5 and s8/s9 boundaries (traced), so these are the MA output stages; group carry logic believed here too. Cells not traced
MA line bundle: nine vertical metal tracks between the left column and the MA output drivers; lines step from track to track
upper rows (9 x 477 px): nine identical rows of another type, extra 87 px after the fourth. Not traced
block right of the upper rows: not surveyed

svg.text: block right of the upper rows ?

rect.title: AND chain column of the mid-right array: per row: x(N) = x(N+1) AND q(N), rippling upward (bottom row first) in groups r0-r6, r7-r10, r11-r14, r15-r18; plus one inverter per row (n1 = NOT p3)

svg.text: AND chain column of the mid-right array

rect.title: group line A (rows r7-r10): wired NOR of g1 = AND of q of rows r7-r10, feeds the chain input of row r6
group line B (rows r15-r18): wired NOR of g1 = AND of q of rows r15-r18 with its load at the bottom, feeds the chain input of row r14

chain input column of the mid-right array: per row: inverter g1 = NOT q, a hold device (gate at VSS) between q and a net z, and a network on the row line m gated by the chain value, its inverse and NOT q; q comes in from the wiring channel on the right; VCC rail x 12412-12462 and signal line A x 12276-12294 run through

svg.text: chain input column of the mid-right array

rect.title: clocked column of the mid-right array, left part: per row: nb = NOT m; node na with a load, pulled low by ck_a (line x 12587) and joined to node u by a ck_b pass gate (line x 12500); VSS rail x 12696-12744; q, p3, n1 pass through

svg.text: clocked column of the mid-right array, left part

rect.title: clocked column of the mid-right array, right part: not traced: per row two large pass transistors (one on ck_b from the line x 12902, one on the ck_a rail x 13025), nodes A and B on the lines x 12815 and 12860, a large poly plate; rail x 12936-12978

svg.text: clocked column of the mid-right array, right part ?

rect.title: wiring channel right of the mid-right array: seven vertical metal lines at 43.5 px that start and stop at different rows (contacts in r0, r3, r4, r10, r14-r18); row outputs cross under it in poly; not traced

svg.text: wiring channel right of the mid-right array

rect.title: R0 register (8 bit): horizontal total; latches loaded from the data lines by sel_w0; feeds the two comparators above
Comparator c = R0 (8 bit): XOR per bit and wired NOR; output south on bundle track L2 (end of line if c is the horizontal counter)
Comparator c = R0 shifted one bit (7 bit): c of each slice against the R0 bit of the next slice, bit 7 of c not compared (believed c = R0/2, the interlace half line); output south on bundle track L0

svg.text: Comparator c = R0 shifted one bit (7 bit)

rect.title: Routing column beside comparator D: exit lines of both comparators, R0 bit 7 going north and round the array, poly bars from the bundle to tracks going north
Left-edge bundle L0..L8: continues rdp3's; the two comparator outputs join it here
R4 register (7 bit): vertical total; latches loaded by sel_w4 (strobe comes up bundle track L1); feeds the comparator above
Comparator uc = R4 (7 bit): XOR per bit and wired NOR against the upper array's seven c lines (believed the row counter); output leaves west at y 8339
?Register RF (7 bit): same latch cells on the same data lines as R4; strobe leaves west at y 8295; its comparator is above (rdp1)
Routing zone between the two arrays: horizontal poly lines; carries R0 bit 7 (y 9487) and comparator D's output (y 9532); otherwise not traced

svg.text: Routing zone between the two arrays

rect.title: Address register (5 bit latch): five transparent latch bits loaded from bus lines s1..s5 when rdp3_ar_ld (areg_load) is high; outputs ar0..ar4 leave to the right
Address register outputs: the five latch outputs running right to the area beside the decode array

R1 register, horizontal displayed (8 bit latch): same latch cell as the address register, upside down; written from the bus lines when sel_w1 is high (strobe followed down bundle track L11, jog to L10 at y 14000, to bd1's sel_w1)

svg.text: R1 register, horizontal displayed (8 bit latch)

rect.title: R1 comparator, XOR row: per slice x = c XOR q (two gates, 7 transistors) of the R1 bit and the per-slice line c
R1 comparator, match line: wired NOR of the eight XORs on a row-wide diffusion line (rdp3_ca_eq, high when R1 = c); load and exit in slice s1; leaves west in poly, then south on the bundle
R2 register, horizontal sync position (8 bit latch): written from the bus lines when sel_w2 is high (strobe followed down the bundle, which steps one track left at y 12357, to bd1's sel_w2)

svg.text: R2 register, horizontal sync position (8 bit latch)

rect.title: R2 comparator, XOR row: per slice x = c XOR q of the R2 bit and the per-slice line c
R2 comparator, match line: wired NOR of the eight XORs (rdp3_cb_eq, high when R2 = c); load and exit in slice s1; leaves west in poly, then north on the bundle
R2 match line exit: poly line from the buried contact in slice s1 west to bundle track L3
R1 match line exit: poly line from the buried contact in slice s1 west to bundle track L3
Bus and c-line routing: poly cross-unders: bus lines s0, s5, s6, s7 leave to the lower right (s0 also goes up the right edge on x 16838); the eight c lines leave to the lower left

Left-edge bundle: twelve vertical tracks stepping one place left at y 12300-12540: write strobes sel_w0 (to R0 above), sel_w2, sel_w1, sel_w4 coming up; R2 match going north, R1 match going south; four c lines going south
select lines leave the decode array: each rselN crosses under the VSS rail in poly and continues on a metal line (or in poly) to its gate

svg.text: select lines leave the decode array

rect.title: write strobes R0-R11: 12 x (inverter + NOR): sel_wN = rselN AND NOT strobe. Left half top to bottom R1 R2 R0 R4 R6 R7, right half R10 R5 R3 R8 R9 R11
left bundle: rsel7 rsel6 rsel4 rsel0 rsel2 down to their gates; strobes of R1 R2 R0 R4 R6 back up and out to the west in poly
middle bundle (16 tracks): selects down to the gates, strobes of R10 R5 R3 R8 R9 R11 down; rsel12 rsel13 pass through; taps to the right-hand column
select buffers R16 R17 R15 R14: two inverters each; the buffered selects go down tracks T11-T14 (?read enables)

svg.text: select buffers R16 R17 R15 R14

rect.title: write strobes R15, R14: inverter + NOR with the strobe, as in the gate column; outputs down T10, T9
gating for datapath line tc1_f: five static gates: f = a.NOT b + b.NOT a.NOT g + a.b.NOT i, and NOT a. f and a are poly lines into the datapath at y 3355 and y 3395. Signals not yet identified
2-bit decode drivers: NOT b; two strong NOR drivers giving (NOT a AND b) and (a AND b); NOR of the first with line W1. Outputs leave by the channel on the west
channel lines W1-W4: four metal verticals serving the island; three are cut where a gate is inserted (a/NOT a/b/NOT b in, driver outputs out, all continuing south)
VSS strap: joins the two outer rails of the island; the poly lines a and b run west under it
island to datapath wiring: metal verticals joining the gates to each other, to the datapath and to the bus field below

six north-south lines ns1-ns6: ns1 = island input w1 (from logic at the datapath slice-0 position); ns2 from the west bus; ns3, ns4, ns6 from over the datapath, ns3/ns4 on south to tc2; ns5, ns6 tap polys going east. No transistors
channel west of the island: four more vertical metals with poly taps into the gate columns; carries l4_out north and the g poly west; mostly untraced
gate columns: dense random logic with large devices under wide rails; not traced. At 6750,3930:6940,4200 a big driver gated by g and by the metal x 6808-6828
top bus field: seven horizontal metal lines crossing the VSS rail in poly; y 2771 = w1/ns1, y 2727 = ns2 traced, rest not
three tracks under the island: bring the two driver outputs and one outside signal from the west side to the AND-OR gate's inputs; two are tapped by lines going south
bus field below the island: VCC bus (y 4198-4250) and VSS bus (y 4288-4335) turning south; b, g, i arrive from tc2; l2_out, l3_out leave south and (l3_out) east; two through lines datapath to tc2
ck_out left-edge trunk: NOT CLK up the left edge of the left array (x 2504); followed closely only below y 18300
ck_out bottom trunk: NOT CLK along the bottom of the core (y 18947), from the clock block to the bottom-left corner
ck_out feed to bottom-centre logic: two wide poly links and a metal line carry NOT CLK to the ring at 10300-10450 x 18340-18485
ck_out rail: NOT CLK at the left edge of the logic below the decode array, fed by a wide poly from x 13131
ck_a rail: clock phase A up the right edge of the mid-right array, one tap per row
clock verticals: ck_b (x 13022), ck_a (x 13066), ck_out (x 13132) crossing the bus field
S in the left bus field: output of input-row gate 0 (NOT X, clock-like): innermost line of the bundle, then x 6862

svg.text: S in the left bus field

rect.title: S along the bottom bus field: middle one of three bus lines, with three poly links

svg.text: S along the bottom bus field

rect.title: E, R/W, RS, CS to the core: e_b (metal, nested corner), rw_d / rs_d / cs_d (diagonal polys, then verticals at x 16298, 16342, 16385)

svg.text: E, R/W, RS, CS to the core

rect.title: RES and LPSTB to the core: res_b (y 2140) and lpstb_b (y 2095), then down a channel at x 5277 / 5320

svg.text: RES and LPSTB to the core

rect.title: CLK pin to the bottom row: CLK pin node in wide poly and metal to the cell row above the CUDISP pad

svg.text: CLK pin to the bottom row

rect.title: cell row fed by CLK: three large U-shaped poly gates driven directly by the CLK pin node; not traced
